newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma confident on ASEAN membership decision.
newsitem.headline: Burma confident on ASEAN membership decision.

text.p: Burma said on Friday it was confident the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) would not be swayed by outside interference as it decides this weekend on when to admit the country as a member.
"Myanmar (Burma) is confident that the ASEAN member countries will collectively decide on what is good for the region as a whole," a senior government spokesman told Reuters.
ASEAN groups Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, the Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam.
Its foreign ministers meet in Malaysia on Saturday to decide when to admit current observers Burma, Cambodia and Laos into the group.

Malaysia, this year's ASEAN chairman, has pressed for the three to be inducted at the association's annual ministerial meeting, scheduled for July 24-25. Another proposal is to admit them at an informal ASEAN summit in December.

But the United States has asked ASEAN to delay Burma's entry because of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council's (SLORC) poor human rights record and suppression of the opposition led by pro-democracy proponent Aung San Suu Kyi.
But ASEAN nations have objected to what they see as Washington's interference in its affairs.

Diplomats and analysts have speculated that Rangoon's latest swoop on the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) ahead of a planned special party gathering and recent clashes between Buddhists and minority Moslems could persuade the ASEAN ministers to delay Burma's membership.
"ASEAN leaders have already proven their wisdom by successfully bringing in nations with different ideologies and religions together to create a strong association in the region," the spokesman said.

"Almost all ASEAN members and the three observer status nations have been former western colonies in the past..." he added. "We believe that the ASEAN members will decide the future of the region on their own wisdom without giving in to outside interference." SLORC has kept the NLD on a tight leash and thwarted its attempts to hold big gatherings.

The government, using armed riot police, on Monday and Tuesday prevented NLD members from gathering at Suu Kyi's home to mark the seventh anniversary of the party's 1990 landslide election win, which was not recognised by SLORC.

The opposition alleged that SLORC had detained 316 party members, including about 50 members of parliament, who the NLD says were arrested in a nationwide swoop to stop the congress taking place. SLORC has denied the charge and asked the opposition to prove its claim.
Another official source had said earlier on Friday that Burma would bar entry to Suu Kyi's home and blockade her party's headquarters until after the ASEAN membership meeting.
He said the military government wanted to avoid clashes with members of the NLD which has urged ASEAN not to admit Burma.
The government spokesman said the NLD had deliberately called a gathering a few days before the ASEAN meeting to create unnecessary problems.
"Is it because of the ASEAN meeting the NLD had to create 'just in time' unnecessary problems in the country for propaganda purposes?" he said.
